A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original gradient-alignment measurements on 410 TREX factual/negated query pairs using three LLMs, presented in Figures 2 and 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those measurements and adds an experiment comparing predicted and actual parameter-update effects on 100 instances in Appendix A.2 and Table 1.

M1.justification: No proposed algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference procedure changes. The normalized-gradient updates added in Appendix A.2 are an experimental diagnostic, not a new adaptation method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the TREX subset of NEGATED LAMA. The added diagnostic reuses factual queries from this dataset; its sample size and update-size sweep change the experimental procedure without adding a dataset, domain, or query task.

E2.justification: The retained alignment experiment examines the same three LLMs. No competing editing methods are newly evaluated; ROME and MEMIT remain related-work references. The new experiment checks a Taylor prediction against actual updates.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a protocol using Qwen3-4B-Instruct, 100 instances, layer-10 target-logit gradients, and normalized-gradient updates at five step sizes from 10^-5 to 10^-1. It evaluates predicted versus actual logit changes using regression slope and R-squared. The original alignment protocol is retained.

E4.justification: The new step-size sensitivity analysis tests when the first-order update approximation remains accurate and when it breaks down. The existing analysis across model scales and architectures is retained, although its former Appendix A.2 heading is incorporated into A.1.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces linear-regression estimation across instances, reporting fitted slopes and R-squared. This adds a statistical estimation procedure, but neither repeated-run information nor confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports slopes 0.97, 1.00, 0.99, 0.89, and 0.21 for increasing step sizes, with R-squared above 0.99 for the first three, then 0.98 and 0.19. These are new validation results. The original gradient-similarity means of 0.85, 0.86, and 0.62 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix F extends the conjunction-collapse argument to approximate negation. For a unit-norm feature and bilinear operator norm M, it derives 2 <= epsilon(1 + 2M + M epsilon), requiring epsilon approximately 0.56 or greater when M = 1. This is a limited quantitative extension; the existing main theorems and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about tensor factorization, converse parity alignment, conjunction collapse, and possible shared geometric origins of editing and reasoning failures.

C2.justification: Section 6 now explicitly distinguishes stepwise applicability under approximately fixed NTK/lazy-training features from nonlocal optimization that changes those features. Section 4 adds discussion of approximate-negation robustness and failure of kernel stability; Appendix A.2 interprets the observed boundary of the linear approximation.

D1.justification: The added diagnostic specifies its model, sample count, layer, gradient normalization, prediction formula, and update sizes. These document a new experiment rather than revise the original alignment implementation. Existing PyTorch, hardware, and runtime disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chizat, Oyallon, and Bach (2019) to support its discussion of lazy training. The broader research positioning remains stable. Changes to the Dummit–Foote and Tarski entries concern the same cited works rather than new literature.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanations and notation footnotes, reorganizes Appendix A, appends Appendix F, and expands the scope discussion. It also corrects 'linear operator' to 'bilinear operation' and updates affiliation, publication, and funding text. The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 with step size, slope, and R-squared columns. Figures 1–4 retain their content and presentation. Added text and the table cause page reflow without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new update-size experiment provides direct support for the practical relevance of the first-order approximation, while Appendix F addresses sensitivity to exact negation assumptions. The clearer discussion of local versus nonlocal applicability also improves precision. These are useful but limited gains: the experiment covers one model on existing data, and the robustness extension retains restrictive bilinear and idempotence assumptions.
